ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The first attempts to describe guest-induced flexibility in zeolites were done using molecular dynamics simulations. $ ^{79-82} $ Rigid zeolitic force fields were dynamically modified using transition state theory to include lattice flexibility, and the results obtained by these models were in good agreement with experimental data. $ ^{79-81,83,84} $ It was shown that framework flexibility in silicalite-1 (MFI-type framework) is responsible for the adsorption of large molecules such as isobutane and heptane with inflection behavior at high loadings, $ ^{80} $ while enhanced self-diffusivity at low loadings of short alkanes (i.e. methane and n-butane) was observed. $ ^{81} $ Framework flexibility is also crucial for aromatics adsorption on MFI zeolite, especially at high pressures. $ ^{84,85} $ While the use of rigid zeolitic models led to the underestimation of the aromatics adsorption in MFI zeolite by a factor of two, $ ^{84,85} $ the use of flexible models to simulate diffusion coefficients of various alkanes in silicalite-1 zeolite resulted in a convergence of experimental and theoretical values. $ ^{86} $ Recently by using in situ integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC-STEM) while adsorbing benzene molecules on MFI zeolite, Xiong et al. showed that the MFI structure goes through severe deformations giving another proof of guest-induced flexibility in zeolites (see Fig. 4). $ ^{87} $

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

descriptor_candidates.name: channel_uniformity_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: For pure-silica zeolites, the fraction of gas-phase entropy retained upon adsorption (s_ads/s_gas) decreases as the pore-limiting diameter approaches the largest free-sphere diameter, i.e., as log(lsd_p/lsd_f) approaches 0. Frameworks with nearly uniform tight channels (ratio near 1) restrict both translation and rotation of the guest, producing larger entropy loss/R than frameworks with large cavities connected by narrow windows (ratio well below 1), where guests retain near-free rotation inside cages.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from confinement theory: translational freedom is lost first in pore apertures while rotational freedom survives in cavities. When lsd_f ≈ lsd_p the guest experiences confinement everywhere (TON/FER-like channels → large entropy loss, cf. E01); when lsd_f >> lsd_p (FAU-like cages, cf. E01) the molecule rotates freely in the cage and loses less entropy. The log compresses the ratio into a smooth descriptor comparable across frameworks.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if, in regression on the dataset, MAE(entropy_loss/R) of the neural network augmented with this descriptor is not reduced relative to the 14-input baseline, or if the fitted/learned dependence has the wrong sign (more entropy loss for cage-window frameworks than for uniform-channel frameworks at matched AV).

descriptor_candidates.name: guest_asphericity_penalty
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss upon adsorption increases with the asphericity of the adsorbate molecule as measured by SPAN/GeDi: elongated guests lose a larger fraction of their gas-phase entropy than compact guests of the same volume, because elongated molecules have more low-energy orientational states in the gas phase that are quenched inside a pore, and their rotational modes freeze out even in cavities.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from statistical mechanics of confined rotors: entropy loss decomposes into translational and rotational contributions (E01, E02, E06). Rotational entropy loss is largest for molecules with a large ratio of largest to smallest body dimension; SPAN (max caliper extent) over GeDi (geometric diameter, smallest enclosing-sphere scale) is a dimension-free asphericity index computable from the given inputs. Shape-selective adsorption of linear vs branched alkanes (E05) shows shape strongly modulates confined adsorption states.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if adding this descriptor does not lower MAE(entropy_loss/R) versus the baseline, or if the learned coefficient shows compact (near-spherical) molecules losing more entropy than elongated ones at equal Vol and equal framework confinement — which would contradict the rotational freeze-out mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: void_fraction_dilution
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: The retained entropy fraction s_ads/s_gas increases with the framework's void fraction (AV multiplied by the framework density on its native source scale): in highly porous, large-cavity frameworks the guest samples a larger free volume and retains more translational entropy, so entropy loss/R decreases roughly logarithmically with void fraction. The +0.01 constant guards the logarithm for near-zero void fractions without introducing a fitted parameter.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Partially established relation: occupiable/free volume as a single descriptor of confined entropy is a known literature result (E03, which used V_occ alone). Reformulating it as AV*density (void volume per framework volume) inside the nonlinear network is a re-expression of existing information, classified as a known_relation rather than a discovery claim; the hypothesis here is that this volume term and the geometric confinement terms above carry partially independent entropy information.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if the network with all three descriptors does not outperform the 14-input baseline in MAE(entropy_loss/R), or if the partial dependence of entropy loss on AV*density is flat or positive (larger void fraction → larger entropy loss), contradicting the free-volume mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_mismatch_asymmetry
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R grows with a product of guest-to-pore size mismatch and guest surface-area-to-volume-shape ratio: molecules whose cubic-volume length scale (Vol^(1/3)) greatly exceeds the pore-limiting diameter lsd_p must compress their configurational space into a quasi-1D channel, and guests with high accessible-surface-to-volume ratio (LabuteASA / Vol^(2/3), a concavity/branchedness index) possess more surface-exposed orientational states that are quenched inside the pore. The multiplicative form predicts that the confinement penalty is largest when both conditions co-occur (bulky, concave guest in a tight channel) and smallest for compact guests in wide pores.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from confinement statistical mechanics: translational entropy loss scales with the ratio of accessible pore volume to free volume, which is governed by the mismatch between guest size and pore-limiting diameter (E01: TON worst, FAU best). The ASA/Vol^(2/3) factor captures branched-vs-linear shape effects on retained rotational states (E01, E05: shape selectivity shows shape strongly modulates confined adsorption states). Unlike round-1's SPAN/GeDi (a pure asphericity index, which did not improve the baseline), this descriptor couples asphericity to framework confinement, testing the interaction rather than the main effect.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if the network augmented with this descriptor does not reduce MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.55608 (round-2 reference), or if the learned partial dependence of entropy loss on the product term is negative (bulky concave guests in tight channels lose LESS entropy), contradicting the confinement-quenching mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: anisotropic_pore_cage_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: The retained entropy fraction s_ads/s_gas decreases with a combined descriptor of framework channel anisotropy: PMI3/PMI1 (perpendicular moment ratio of the guest, near 1 for isotropic molecules, large for elongated ones) times lsd_f/lsd_p (framework cage-to-window expansion, near 1 for uniform channels, large for cage-window topologies). The hypothesis is that entropy loss is governed by the interaction between guest anisotropy and framework topology: elongated molecules in cage-window frameworks (large product, e.g., FAU-like hosts with long guests) can adopt many distinct low-energy cage configurations and lose relatively little entropy per rotational degree, whereas spherical guests in uniform tight channels (small product) lose near-complete translational and rotational freedom. Note this predicts the opposite sign for the cage-window factor alone than for elongated guests — an explicitly falsifiable interaction claim.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from confined-rotor statistics and diffusion anisotropy (E01: entropy loss decomposes into translational and rotational contributions differing by framework; E09: molecular symmetry modulates confined dynamics differently in cages vs channels). The descriptor mixes guest rotational inertia asymmetry (PMI3/PMI1, derived from PMI1 and PMI3 inputs) with the cage-window geometric contrast (lsd_f/lsd_p) to test whether framework topology and guest anisotropy carry non-redundant entropy information beyond the additive terms tried in round 1.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if the descriptor does not improve MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.55608, or if the learned dependence shows no interaction (e.g., the network is insensitive to the product while responding to each factor alone), indicating PMI3/PMI1 and lsd_f/lsd_p carry only redundant information already captured by the 14-input baseline.

descriptor_candidates.name: packed_density_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R increases with the guest's own condensed-phase compactness (MW/Vol, a guest liquid-density-like quantity) multiplied by the guest-to-framework accessible-volume ratio (Vol divided by pore volume per framework volume, AV/density on native scales). Molecules that are internally dense and compact (high MW/Vol) have fewer internal conformational states to lose but pay a large translational confinement penalty when their bulk volume fills a substantial fraction of the pore volume; the hypothesis is that fractional occupancy of the free volume by the guest's own volume — not absolute pore size — sets the residual vibrational-librational entropy of the adsorbed state.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E03 established V_occ (framework occupiable volume) alone as a single descriptor of entropy loss (known_relation); this proposal tests the complementary, still-unencoded side — the guest's volumetric footprint relative to that free volume, combined with the guest's intrinsic density, which determine how much of the free volume remains unexplored and hence how much translational entropy survives. Unlike the retained void_fraction_dilution (framework-only term), this is a guest-framework ratio, a distinct mechanism (fractional occupation of free volume). Source evidence covers the free-volume side (E01, E03); the guest-compactness interaction is inference.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if adding this descriptor fails to lower MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.55608, or if partial dependence shows entropy loss decreasing with guest-volume/pore-volume ratio at matched void fraction — which would contradict the fractional-occupancy free-volume mechanism and indicate the retained void fraction term already saturates this information.

descriptor_candidates.name: window_bottleneck_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R is governed jointly by the aperture bottleneck and the total free volume: the retained entropy fraction s_ads/s_gas falls as (lsd_p/lsd_f)^2 (fraction of the cage-scale dimension still open at the window, penalizing translational freedom at the aperture) but rises with the square root of void fraction. The descriptor predicts that at equal void fraction, cage-window frameworks (small lsd_p/lsd_f) lose more entropy than uniform-channel frameworks, and that at equal window ratio, denser frameworks lose more entropy. This is an interaction claim: the aperture penalty is amplified in low-void frameworks.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 shows translational entropy loss dominates in tight apertures (TON worst, FAU best) and E03 shows occupiable volume alone is a single-descriptor predictor (known_relation). The proposal is inference: combining the aperture-cage contrast with void fraction as a multiplicative bottleneck assumes the window, not the cavity, controls the partition-function reduction, i.e., a transition-state-like bottleneck mechanism rather than a purely volumetric one.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if the network augmented with this descriptor does not reduce MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.54653 (round-3 reference), or if the learned partial dependence shows entropy loss decreasing with decreasing lsd_p/lsd_f at matched void fraction (larger windows → more entropy loss), contradicting the bottleneck mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: inertial_shape_surface_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R increases with the product of the guest's two orthogonal inertial anisotropy ratios and its surface-to-volume shape factor: (PMI2*PMI1... specifically PMI2*PMI3/PMI1^2) exceeds 1 for molecules elongated or flattened out of isotropy, and such molecules have multiple distinguishable rotor orientations in the gas phase that collapse onto nearly degenerate confined states inside a pore. Coupled to LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3), which measures how much of the molecular surface is exposed and hence how many wall-contact geometries exist, the descriptor predicts that high-surface-area anisotropic guests freeze the most rotational entropy, independently of volume alone.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 and E06 decompose entropy loss into translational and rotational contributions, with rotational freeze-out depending on molecular shape; E09 shows molecular symmetry modulates confined dynamics. Round-1's SPAN/GeDi (caliper-based asphericity) failed to improve the baseline, suggesting caliper ratios carry redundant information; principal moments are a different, inertia-based encoding of the same shape space, and coupling them to the surface-exposure index tests whether rotational quenching is surface-contact driven rather than purely geometric. This coupling is inference.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if adding this descriptor does not lower MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.54653, or if partial dependence shows near-isotropic molecules (PMI2*PMI3/PMI1^2 ≈ 1) losing MORE entropy than anisotropic ones at matched LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3) and framework, contradicting the rotational-quenching mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: volumetric_footprint_pore_match
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R grows logarithmically with the guest's linear footprint per unit pore dimension: Vol normalized by the framework's pore volume per framework volume (AV/density on the native scale) gives a guest-volume-per-pore-volume measure, and dividing by lsd_p converts this into a length-scale ratio between the guest's effective bulk extent and the pore-limiting diameter. The hypothesis is that entropy loss is set not by any absolute size but by how many pore-diameter-lengths of translational freedom the guest's own volume occupies — guests whose normalized footprint is large are already near close-packing in the pore and lose almost all translational entropy, while small guests in voluminous pores retain a gas-like fraction.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 (framework-dependent entropy loss scaling with confinement) and E03 (single-descriptor V_occ prediction of entropy loss, a known_relation) establish the volumetric confinement framework; E05 shows shape/size matching dictates adsorption states. The specific re-expression as a logarithmic length-scale ratio combining guest Vol, framework AV*density, and lsd_p is new inference: it tests whether a dimensionally consistent (length/length) confinement measure outperforms purely volumetric or purely caliper-based descriptors tried in earlier rounds.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if the network with this descriptor does not improve MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.54653, or if the learned partial dependence is flat or negative (larger footprint-per-pore-diameter → less entropy loss), which would contradict the fractional-occupancy translational-quenching mechanism and indicate the retained void_fraction_dilution and shape_mismatch_asymmetry terms already saturate the volumetric confinement information.

candidates.name: window_bottleneck_ratio
candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R is governed jointly by the aperture bottleneck and the total free volume: the retained entropy fraction s_ads/s_gas falls as (lsd_p/lsd_f)^2 (fraction of the cage-scale dimension still open at the window, penalizing translational freedom at the aperture) but rises with the square root of void fraction. The descriptor predicts that at equal void fraction, cage-window frameworks (small lsd_p/lsd_f) lose more entropy than uniform-channel frameworks, and that at equal window ratio, denser frameworks lose more entropy. This is an interaction claim: the aperture penalty is amplified in low-void frameworks.
candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 shows translational entropy loss dominates in tight apertures (TON worst, FAU best) and E03 shows occupiable volume alone is a single-descriptor predictor (known_relation). The proposal is inference: combining the aperture-cage contrast with void fraction as a multiplicative bottleneck assumes the window, not the cavity, controls the partition-function reduction, i.e., a transition-state-like bottleneck mechanism rather than a purely volumetric one.
candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if the network augmented with this descriptor does not reduce MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.54653 (round-3 reference), or if the learned partial dependence shows entropy loss decreasing with decreasing lsd_p/lsd_f at matched void fraction (larger windows → more entropy loss), contradicting the bottleneck mechanism.

candidates.name: inertial_shape_surface_index
candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R increases with the product of the guest's two orthogonal inertial anisotropy ratios and its surface-to-volume shape factor: (PMI2*PMI1... specifically PMI2*PMI3/PMI1^2) exceeds 1 for molecules elongated or flattened out of isotropy, and such molecules have multiple distinguishable rotor orientations in the gas phase that collapse onto nearly degenerate confined states inside a pore. Coupled to LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3), which measures how much of the molecular surface is exposed and hence how many wall-contact geometries exist, the descriptor predicts that high-surface-area anisotropic guests freeze the most rotational entropy, independently of volume alone.
candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 and E06 decompose entropy loss into translational and rotational contributions, with rotational freeze-out depending on molecular shape; E09 shows molecular symmetry modulates confined dynamics. Round-1's SPAN/GeDi (caliper-based asphericity) failed to improve the baseline, suggesting caliper ratios carry redundant information; principal moments are a different, inertia-based encoding of the same shape space, and coupling them to the surface-exposure index tests whether rotational quenching is surface-contact driven rather than purely geometric. This coupling is inference.
candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if adding this descriptor does not lower MAE(entropy_loss/R) below 0.54653, or if partial dependence shows near-isotropic molecules (PMI2*PMI3/PMI1^2 ≈ 1) losing MORE entropy than anisotropic ones at matched LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3) and framework, contradicting the rotational-quenching mechanism.

retained.name: void_fraction_dilution
retained.hypothesis: The retained entropy fraction s_ads/s_gas increases with the framework's void fraction (AV multiplied by the framework density on its native source scale): in highly porous, large-cavity frameworks the guest samples a larger free volume and retains more translational entropy, so entropy loss/R decreases roughly logarithmically with void fraction. The +0.01 constant guards the logarithm for near-zero void fractions without introducing a fitted parameter.

retained.name: shape_mismatch_asymmetry
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R grows with a product of guest-to-pore size mismatch and guest surface-area-to-volume-shape ratio: molecules whose cubic-volume length scale (Vol^(1/3)) greatly exceeds the pore-limiting diameter lsd_p must compress their configurational space into a quasi-1D channel, and guests with high accessible-surface-to-volume ratio (LabuteASA / Vol^(2/3), a concavity/branchedness index) possess more surface-exposed orientational states that are quenched inside the pore. The multiplicative form predicts that the confinement penalty is largest when both conditions co-occur (bulky, concave guest in a tight channel) and smallest for compact guests in wide pores.
